title: Own Tasks with JoinSet
concept: Completion order, errors, and task lifetime

writing.summary: Keep the tasks you start in a collection whose lifetime and results are explicit.
writing.rule: Spawning starts an independent task; awaiting its result is a separate responsibility.
writing.explanation:
An async function creates a future, while spawning places that future under a runtime's scheduler. If your operation starts several child tasks, decide who owns their handles and who observes failures. JoinSet groups tasks returning the same type and yields their results in completion order. That order is not necessarily the order in which the tasks were inserted.

The example associates each result with its input index, drains the set with join_next, and sorts the collected pairs before presenting them. The sorting is a deliberate presentation policy, not an assumption about scheduler order. Handle the outer JoinError separately from any application Result returned inside a task: a task panic and a rejected input are different failures.

Dropping a JoinSet aborts its remaining tasks. This makes ownership visible, but abort is not a business-level rollback and does not undo effects already performed. A spawned blocking operation can have additional cancellation limitations. A reliable operation either drains its children, cancels them according to an explicit policy, or transfers their ownership to a longer-lived component.

Desktop Cargo profile: use `tokio = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["rt", "sync"] }`. These examples build a current-thread runtime explicitly and need no Tokio procedural macros, sockets, timers, signals, or multi-thread scheduler. A current-thread executor can run concurrent futures but does not provide CPU parallelism. In Crabrix, consult the prepared Cargo compatibility report before running the project; this reading is not a promise that every Tokio feature works in a WASI guest.

For practice, make one child return an application error without panicking. Then make a different child panic and compare the two error layers. Do not require an exact completion sequence in the test; verify the set of indexed results. Keep real network work out of this exercise so scheduling behavior is not confused with a server or a backend execution service.

writing.success: JoinSet yields completed tasks. Preserve an index if the application needs a stable presentation order.
writing.question: In which order does JoinSet yield completed tasks?
answers: Completion order, which may differ from insertion order
writing.feedback: JoinSet yields completed tasks. Preserve an index if the application needs a stable presentation order.

depth.misconception: Dropping every task handle is a graceful shutdown protocol.
depth.correction: An explicit owner must decide whether to wait, request cancellation, or abort; prior effects are not rolled back.

traceSteps.title: Finish
traceSteps.detail: Drain results or explicitly cancel remaining tasks.

depth.transferChallenge: Document what happens when one task fails after another has written a report. Do not describe abort as rollback.
